title: Perimeter and Area: Triangles, Parallelograms, Trapezia and Compound Shapes
seo_title: Year 7 Area and Perimeter Worksheets: Triangles, Parallelograms, Trapezia and Compound Shapes
standard_text: Derive and apply formulae to calculate and solve problems involving: perimeter and area of triangles, parallelograms, trapezia, volume of cuboids (including cubes) and other prisms (including cylinders); calculate and solve problems involving: perimeters of 2-D shapes (including circles), areas of circles and composite shapes.
meta_desc: Free Year 7 area and perimeter worksheets with diagrams: rectangles, triangles, parallelograms, trapezia, missing sides, L-shaped compound shapes and real-life problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Triangle area = ½ × base × perpendicular height. Trapezium area = ½(a + b)h.
key_sub: Use the perpendicular height, not the slanted side. Area is in square units, perimeter in units of length.
body_html:
How it works

Perimeter is the distance all the way round a shape (cm). Area is the space inside (cm²).

  • Rectangle: area = length × width
  • Triangle: area = ½ × base × perpendicular height
  • Parallelogram: area = base × perpendicular height
  • Trapezium: area = ½(a + b)h

The height must be perpendicular (at right angles) to the base, not the slanted side. For a compound shape, split it into rectangles, or take a piece away from a bigger rectangle.

Example

Find the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and perpendicular height 6 cm.

½ × 10 × 6 = 30.

Answer: 30 cm²

Example

Find the area of a trapezium with parallel sides 4 cm and 8 cm and height 5 cm.

½ × (4 + 8) × 5 = ½ × 12 × 5.

Answer: 30 cm²

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to halve for a triangle: base × height gives double the area.
  • Using the slanted side instead of the perpendicular height.
  • Mixing up area and perimeter, or writing cm instead of cm².
  • Missing a side when finding the perimeter of an L-shape: there are 6 sides.

faq.q: What is the formula for the area of a trapezium?
faq.a: Area = ½(a + b)h, where a and b are the parallel sides and h is the perpendicular height.

faq.q: Why do we halve for the area of a triangle?
faq.a: A triangle is half of a rectangle (or parallelogram) with the same base and height.

faq.q: What is the difference between area and perimeter?
faq.a: Perimeter is the distance around the edge, measured in cm or m. Area is the space inside, measured in cm² or m².

faq.q: How do I find the area of an L-shape?
faq.a: Split it into two rectangles and add their areas, or find the big rectangle and take away the missing corner.

A square has an area of 64 cm². What is its perimeter?
items.e: Side = √64 = 8 cm, so perimeter = 4 × 8 = 32 cm.

items.q: A square has a perimeter of 36 cm. What is its area?
items.e: Side = 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm, so area = 9 × 9 = 81 cm².

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 72 cm² and a width of 6 cm. What is its length?
items.e: Length = 72 ÷ 6 = 12 cm.

Square tiles of side 50 cm cover a floor 4 m by 3 m. How many tiles are needed?
items.e: 4 m = 8 tiles and 3 m = 6 tiles, so 8 × 6 = 48 tiles.

items.q: Which has the larger area: a 6 cm by 6 cm square or a 9 cm by 4 cm rectangle?
items.e: Square: 36 cm². Rectangle: 36 cm². They have the same area (but different perimeters: 24 cm and 26 cm).

items.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 20 cm. Which of these could be its area?
items.e: Length + width = 10. For example 6 × 4 = 24 cm². The largest possible area is 5 × 5 = 25 cm², so 40 and 100 are impossible.

Which units are used for area?
items.e: Area is measured in square units such as cm² and m².

items.q: A parallelogram has base 9 cm and perpendicular height 4 cm. Its slanted side is 5 cm. What is its area?
items.e: Area = base × perpendicular height = 9 × 4 = 36 cm². The 5 cm side is not used.

items.q: A trapezium has parallel sides of 6 cm and 10 cm and a height of 5 cm. What is its area?
How many cm² are in 1 m²?
The area of a rectangle is 48 m². Its length is 3 times its width. What is its width?
Two identical squares are placed side by side to make a rectangle with perimeter 30 cm. What is the side of each square?
items.e: The rectangle is 2s by s, so its perimeter is 6s = 30 and s = 5 cm.

items.q: A path 1 m wide goes round a lawn 10 m by 6 m. What is the area of the path?
items.e: Outside 12 × 8 = 96 m². Lawn 10 × 6 = 60 m². Path = 96 − 60 = 36 m².
